event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: AMP’s 2024-02-22 Form 10-K continues to frame the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic primarily as a market-wide, macroeconomic hazard rather than a narrowly tailored operational emergency.  Nearly four years after the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic, the company’s language has shifted from crisis response to acknowledging an enduring, but more generalized, source of volatility.  The filing repeatedly cites COVID-19 (often bundled with other disruptions) as a historic trigger of equity, credit-spread and interest-rate swings that "have impacted our business in the past, are impacting us now and may continue to impact us."  These references confirm a still-present, forward-looking risk, but they lack fresh, quantified detail about supply-chain blockage, labour force depletion, or remote-work cost structures.  Given the Time Decay Principle, the pandemic sits at the early edge of the 4-to-10-year “medium-term” window; consequently, even the strongest sentences warrant moderate (not severe) scoring.  The language is partly specific—describing market volatility and annuity valuation stress already experienced—yet it remains largely cautionary rather than reporting new, material impacts.  Overall, the evidence supports moderate risk salience: not negligible but no longer acute, reflecting the pandemic’s ongoing but diffused influence on AMP’s market-sensitive revenue streams and capital requirements.

evidence_list.snippet: Declines and volatility in U.S. and global market conditions (such as those that resulted from the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent economic environment, from other recent geopolitical tensions or from situations like the 2023 regional bank crisis) have impacted our businesses in the past, are impacting us now and may continue to impact us in the same, new or different ways in the future.

components.reason: Explicitly links COVID-19 to actual market declines and volatility.
States impacts are past, current and prospective, confirming ongoing exposure.
Uses broad but still material wording ('have impacted our businesses').
Bundled with other events, slightly diluting COVID-specificity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strongest statement: ties COVID-19 to realised and continuing effects on multiple business lines; medium-term event cap trims score to 6.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, interest rate fluctuations could result in fluctuations in the valuation of certain minimum guaranteed benefits contained in some of our variable annuity products, something we saw as a result of volatility that resulted from the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Describes a specific financial stress (valuation swings in annuity guarantees) already observed because of COVID-19 volatility.
Identifies direct product-level impact rather than generic macro comment.
Framed historically ('we saw'), implying lessons learned rather than unresolved crisis.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete, product-level evidence of COVID-linked volatility but is retrospective, yielding a solid yet moderate 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Such factors, which can be global, regional, national or local in nature, include: (v) the level and volatility of the markets, including equity prices, interest rates, commodity prices, currency values and other market indices and drivers; ... (v) global health emergencies (such as the coronavirus disease 2019 (“COVID-19”) pandemic);

components.reason: Explicitly lists COVID-19 pandemic as a material market-risk driver.
Placement in a long, catch-all list makes the reference generic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Merely catalogues COVID-19 among many factors with no impact detail; minimal aggravation, thus score of 1.

evidence_list.snippet: The occurrence of natural or man-made disasters and catastrophes, including earthquakes, hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, fires, blackouts, severe winter weather, explosions, pandemic disease and global health emergencies (such as COVID-19) ... could adversely affect our results of operations or financial condition.

components.reason: Acknowledges COVID-19 as a potential catastrophe capable of harming results.
Highly conditional ('could'), bundled with many unrelated perils.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic contingency statement with no evidence of actual impact; low severity and thus score remains 1.
